column1: # Bilibin first approach, afflicted citizen, McCoy's failed palace commission, guards and refusal branch.
# Preserve scripted dialogue IDs, runtime actor names and yes/no endings.

column3: It has a face. Those knots\nalmost look like someone\ntrying to speak.{end_wait}
That barricade went up when\nthe trouble in Kolima\nbegan.{end_wait}
The road to Kolima is\nblocked. Lord McCoy ordered\nthe barricade built, and he{page_break}won't let anyone pass.{end_wait}
We built that barricade in\na hurry. It isn't pretty,\nbut it stops most{page_break}travelers.{end_wait}
It's east of here. We had\nto finish before sunset, so\nI cut a few corners.{end_wait}

I've heard sailors talk
about strange lands beyond
the sea. Places where the{page_break}mist never lifts. I'd like
to know if they're real.{end_wait}
I've never seen the ocean.\nThey say it's so wide you\ncan't see the other shore.{page_break}Imagine that.{end_wait}
Did you hear that growl?\nTell me you heard it.{end_now}
Of course I heard it.\nThat's my stomach. I\nhaven't eaten since{page_break}morning!{end_wait}
{text_effect:4}Grrr...{reset_text_style} Where's my dinner?\nMy stomach's been talking\nlonger than I have!{end_wait}
After seeing that man\nturned into a tree, I don't\nknow how anyone can call{page_break}the curse a rumor.{end_wait}
Go ask Lord McCoy, then.\nHe'll tell you what he\nthinks happened.{end_wait}
You seem honest enough. But\nI can't send children into\nmy lord's chambers on a{page_break}promise.{end_wait}
You don't look afraid.\nMaybe I judged you too\nquickly.{end_wait}
They're young. Do we really\nwant to send them into that\nforest?{end_wait}
Every warrior we've hired\nhas vanished. We may not\nhave another choice.{end_wait}
All right. I'll take you to\nLord McCoy. Stay close.{end_wait}
McCoy's furious. He says he\nsent for you an hour ago.{end_wait}
You're the first to\nvolunteer in days. Please,\nhelp us if you can.{end_wait}
He asked you to go into\nKolima? I didn't think he'd\nfind anyone willing.{end_wait}
If you go, don't let the\ndust touch you. I saw what\nhappened to the others.{end_wait}
I hope you know what you're\nagreeing to. I wouldn't go\nthere for any price.{end_wait}
Choose one of these four\ntreasures. It's payment for\ntaking the risk.{end_wait}
The other treasures are\nyours when the job is\nfinished.{end_wait}
My lord, more travelers\nhave come asking to see\nyou.{end_wait}
More warriors, are they?\nBring them here.{end_wait}
We sent good men into\nKolima Forest. Not a one\nhas returned.{end_wait}
Did you look these new\nfellows over? Do they know\nwhat they're facing?{end_wait}
Come closer, lad. Let me\nget a look at you.{end_wait}
These are the travelers you\nwanted me to meet?{end_wait}
They're children! What were\nyou thinking?{end_wait}
You expect me to believe\nyou can break a curse that\nhas beaten trained men?{end_now}
No. I won't send you. Leave\nthe palace.{end_wait}
Here. This key will open\nthe barricade to the east.{end_wait}
A key won't make the forest\nsafe. Don't mistake my help\nfor a promise you'll{page_break}return.{end_wait}
He keeps calling us\nchildren. Are you going to\nlet that stop us, {actor_name:1}?{end_now}
So you'll take the job\nafter all?{end_wait}
{actor_name:3}, you don't sound\nconvinced. What's wrong?{end_wait}
Men have turned into trees\nout there. It's not\nsomething we can fight with{page_break}swords.{end_wait}
We can still try. I'm not\nleaving Kolima like that.{end_wait}
You believe we can do it,\ndon't you, {actor_name:1}?{end_now}
Well, at least we've\nsettled that.{end_wait}
My lord, they're willing to\ntry. What more can we ask?{end_wait}
Willing? They're barely\ngrown! They don't know what\nthey're offering.{end_wait}
Aye, we're desperate. But I\nwon't send children to die\nin a forest I helped ruin.{end_wait}
Then what about Kolima? Do\nwe simply leave those\npeople as trees?{end_wait}
We must hope one of the\nwarriors we've already\nhired returns.{end_wait}
But we're standing right\nhere. We could still help.{end_wait}
No. I won't have your\ndeaths on my conscience as\nwell.{end_wait}
What if we were going east\nanyway? You can't stop us\nfrom traveling.{end_wait}
You can travel when the\nroads are safe. Until then,\nthe barricade stays shut.{end_wait}
So you're refusing to let\nus go?{end_wait}
Aye, lad. You'll live long\nenough to hate me for it.{end_wait}
I've made my decision.\nCaptain, see them out.{end_wait}
I'm sorry. The audience is\nover. Please leave.{end_wait}
I've never seen Bilibin\nthis frightened. People are\nafraid to leave their{page_break}homes.{end_wait}
Promise me you won't try to\nreach Kolima on your own.{end_now}
Good. There's nothing to be\ngained by losing you too.{end_wait}
Still thinking about that\nforest? You really won't\nlet it go.{end_wait}
The barricade is sturdy,\nbut you might not need a\nkey to get past it.{end_wait}
Ah. I shouldn't have told\nyou that.{end_wait}
I have work to do. Please,\nstay out of trouble.{end_wait}
